questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I chose to go on exchange to the University of Melbourne because I had heard great things about Melbourne. The city is a fantastic place to live. Additionally, the university is highly prestigious and ranks well in various rankings.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very easy to get information about the exchange. You are guided by the University of Copenhagen. In addition, you constantly receive emails about the stay, which means you always know what to do.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Guidance from my home university and guidance from the University of Melbourne.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: It was very easy to find accommodation. In Melbourne, there are several different providers that offer housing for students. However, it was also incredibly expensive.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I recommend travelling to Melbourne before finding accommodation. That way, you can view the places in person. I don’t recommend – as I unfortunately did – securing housing from home. Even though it can feel reassuring to arrange accommodation in advance, it’s important to make the right choice. I later found out that I could have gotten much better and even cheaper places.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It was very easy to register. On the website, you can see what to do step by step.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You receive emails, they have a website, and you get guidance from your home university.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes I applied for.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: You don’t need to worry about registration. It will all work out fine. The only thing you need is a bit of patience.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The teaching was satisfactory, but I consciously chose to take undergraduate courses. That made it quite a bit easier.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There was a mix of seminars and lectures, similar to what you’re used to at home. In one of my courses, I had a 75% attendance requirement, which is different from what I’m used to. The exams are quite different from those at the University of Copenhagen, with multiple exams in a single course. You also have to write quite a few essays. However, you don’t need to worry about the level - it will be fine.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Sport and the Law
Legal Language
Environmental Rights and Responsibilities
Principles of Business Law

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Sport and the Law. It was a really great course. The instructors were extremely skilled, the syllabus was engaging, and the exam was a positive experience.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Travel expenses were a significant cost. Additionally, the visa cost 8,000 kroner, which was much more expensive than expected. Unfortunately, the price has increased this year.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Accommodation, visa, and travel expenses

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There are many sports clubs. I was part of the football club and also participated in some of the other sports clubs.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend joining some sports clubs.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Traveling around Australia.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was very easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Not much. People are really kind. If you have an open mind and are friendly, everything will be fine. Of course, there are a few things you need to get used to, but that happens gradually.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People are very friendly.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: I would say that, first and foremost, you should get involved socially. You need to be good at being social and reach out to other exchange students. This will make your stay much better. As I mentioned, I recommend travelling to Melbourne before finding accommodation. That way, you can see the places before choosing where you’ll live. Finally, I suggest you travel around Australia a bit - maybe even arrive well before your exchange starts - so you have plenty of time to explore beautiful Australia and everything it has to offer.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: It was an amazing experience. The best part of it all was the people I met there.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: You are far away from family and friends, and the time difference is also hard to get used to.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
